I don't see a net benefit of an upvoat limit like the one we have for new users. It genuinely takes a while to accumulate 20 CCP to even begin to increase the limit. In the meantime, users are being conditioned to not upvoat content they like, because so often they try and fail. On top of this, they don't have any clear indication of when they will be able to upvoat again. It conditions them to participate less, not more.

Users who don't don't like putting in time to comment will either continue to not comment, or will write a few comments that don't get voated on (although they may have gotten voated up had the barriers not been high) and then stop trying. I'm sure a few will participate more and be optimistic of getting CCP, but many, many users will not. When fewer people can voat, the quality of the content goes down, and people go back to reddit, where they and the people before them can vote.

One thing that I have noticed also in voat is tons of comments getting downvoated despite having no indication of trolling, seemingly only downvoated by frequent users who disagreed with this new user's view. When people with the right idea of what voating means (voat on what people should see, not what you agree with, mostly) can't voat to combat this, it makes the situation worse.

I am not completely opposed to some kind of upvoat limiting, but it cannot be this high. We want to encourage people to say what they think, but putting a high barrier just encourages them to say what everyone thinks. Or leave.

reddit does let you do everything right off the bat--with the exception of subreddits that add their own limitations--but that hasn't caused as many problems as many claim. To me, providing a limit--even a tall one like 100 CCP--for downvoats is a great idea, and one that reddit could benefit from: it makes voating brigades more difficult and provides a significant incentive to participate. On the other hand, I don't see much benefit from restricting upvoats. (Although I might suggest easing users into it with, say, a right to limited upvoats at 30 CCP.) The current restrictions on upvoats seem like one step too far--especially because for new users, upvoats will be their first introduction into the "have your say" internet world. From your comment history, you have participation far above what most users are willing to give, and I think far above most users should be expected to give.
